sources.entry: Gray - Per-app light/dark mode switcher. ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/zenangst/Gray)
Gray - Pick between the light appearance and the dark appearance on a per-app basis with the click of a button

summary.one_liner: Gray is a macOS utility that lets you force individual apps to use the light or dark appearance regardless of the system setting.
summary.what_it_does: Gray lets you choose, for each app, whether it uses the light aqua appearance or the dark appearance, switching with a click. The README explains that it works by setting the app's NSRequiresAquaSystemAppearance default, which forces that app into light mode. The same effect can be achieved manually with a single defaults write terminal command, and the README notes this only adds an entry to the user's preferences without changing anything else on the system. Gray handles restarting the affected app so the change takes effect, and the README asks users to save work first. The README also includes instructions for building the project from source with Xcode and CocoaPods. The README does not describe a detailed feature list beyond this per-app toggle.
use_cases: Keep a light-themed app while the rest of macOS is in dark mode
Force specific apps to light appearance
Set up mixed light and dark windows on the same Mac
Undo a dark appearance for apps that look wrong in dark mode
Build the Gray app from source
how_to_run: Go to System Preferences > General and set the Mac to dark appearance.
Download the latest version (0.17.0) from the Download link in the README.
Optional build from source: git clone git@github.com:zenangst/Gray.git
notable: Per-app light/dark appearance toggle with a single click
Works by setting the NSRequiresAquaSystemAppearance user default, which can be applied manually with a terminal command
Does not modify the system beyond the per-app preference entry, according to the README
Restarts affected apps automatically to apply the change
caveats: Affected apps must restart before changes take effect, so unsaved work should be saved first
Only forces apps into light appearance; the README does not describe other appearance options
The README does not state supported macOS versions
